channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting: When It Helps, When It Hurts
item.description: Chain-of-thought prompting boosts performance on some tasks and quietly degrades it on others. I unpack the mechanism, a worked example, and when to skip it.

item.title: System Prompts vs User Prompts: Where Instructions Belong
item.description: System prompts and user prompts are not interchangeable containers. Where you put an instruction changes how reliably a model follows it.

item.title: Few-Shot Prompts: How Many Examples Is Too Many
item.description: Adding more few-shot examples feels safe, but past a point it wastes tokens, biases outputs, and can quietly hurt accuracy.

item.title: Structured Prompt Templates: Stop Guessing, Start Repeating
item.description: Ad hoc prompting doesn't scale. A structured template with fixed slots makes prompting testable, versionable, and far easier to debug.

item.title: Building a Case Study a Hiring Manager Will Actually Read
item.description: A hiring manager gives your portfolio ten seconds. Structure your case study so it earns the next ninety.

item.title: How Pretraining Data Shapes What a Transformer Can Do
item.description: Architecture gets the credit, but pretraining data quietly decides what a transformer can ever learn to do well.

item.title: Semantic Segmentation vs Object Detection: Pick Wisely
item.description: Segmentation and detection both find objects, but they cost and deliver very different things. Here is how to choose without guessing.

item.title: Data Scientist vs Machine Learning Engineer, in Practice
item.description: Same buzzwords, different jobs. Here's what actually separates data science from ML engineering once you look past the job title.

item.title: Writing Prompts That Survive a Model Upgrade
item.description: Clever prompt tricks decay fast. Here is how to write prompts that keep working when the underlying model changes.

item.title: A Realistic MLOps Syllabus: What To Learn First
item.description: Before you call yourself an MLOps engineer, learn what actually breaks in production: data drift, silent leakage, and pipelines nobody can reproduce.

item.title: Choosing Your First Computer Vision Project Wisely
item.description: Skip the trendy demo. Pick a computer vision project small enough to finish and honest enough to teach you where things actually go wrong.

item.title: Salary Expectations in Data Science: The Untold Work
item.description: Salary surveys flatten wildly different jobs into one number. Here is what the figure hides about the actual work.

item.title: Data Science Degrees vs Portfolios: What Interviews Check
item.description: Degrees and portfolios both signal something, but interviews test neither directly. Here is what actually gets checked.

item.title: How to Read a Confusion Matrix Class by Class
item.description: A model with 94% accuracy can still be useless for the one class you care about. Learn to read confusion matrices row by row, not just the headline number.

item.title: Computer Vision Syndrome vs Evaluating Computer Vision Models
item.description: Computer vision syndrome is eye strain from screens. Model evaluation is how we judge vision systems. Same name, nothing else in common, and the confusion teaches a lesson about precision.

item.title: The Prompt Engineering Skill Set: What Transfers
item.description: Prompt tricks age fast, but the underlying skills of decomposition, evaluation and constraint design do not. Here is how to tell the difference.

item.title: MLOps Tools Compared: Ten Users Versus Ten Thousand
item.description: Most MLOps advice is written for scale you don't have yet. Here's a leakage-aware, honest guide to what to adopt at ten users versus ten thousand.

item.title: Positional Encodings: Why Transformers Need Them at All
item.description: Self-attention is permutation-invariant by default. Without positional encodings, a transformer literally cannot tell 'dog bites man' from 'man bites dog'.

item.title: Sequence Labelling Metrics: Why Token Accuracy Lies
item.description: High token accuracy on sequence labelling tasks can mask a much worse entity-level error rate. Here's the arithmetic that proves it.

item.title: Domain Adaptation Versus Fine-Tuning: Adapting Is Not Retraining
item.description: Fine-tuning a model on new data is not the same as adapting it to a new domain. The difference decides whether your reported gains survive contact with reality.
